# hivelocity_dns_record_mx (Resource)

Manages an MX record in a Hivelocity-hosted zone. Import with `<domain_id>:<record_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hivelocity_dns_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

resource "hivelocity_dns_record_mx" "mail" {
  domain_id  = hivelocity_dns_domain.example.domain_id
  name       = "@"
  exchange   = "mail.example.com"
  preference = 10
  ttl        = 3600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (Number) ID of the zone (`hivelocity_dns_domain.domain_id`).
- `exchange` (String) Mail server host name, for example `mail.example.com`.
- `name` (String) Record name, for example `@` for the zone apex.
- `preference` (Number) Preference (priority) of the mail server; lower is preferred.
- `ttl` (Number) Time to live of the record, in seconds.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `record_id` (Number) Unique ID of the record.
- `type` (String) Record type as reported by the API.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with <domain_id>:<record_id>
terraform import hivelocity_dns_record_mx.mail 1234:5678
```
